Wide painted seascape at dawn, camera low on the beach. A vast flat silver-grey sea, mist on the water, a dark headland. Heo's ship rounds the headland, its one great crimson battened sail swollen full and taut with wind, curved like a body arching (copy the attached ship board for the ship design only: ornate red-and-gold lacquered hull with painted panels, one great crimson battened sail and a small red mizzen; repaint it in dawn light). In the foreground a long, straight timber pier juts far out over the water, pointing straight at the ship, aching toward it, its last planks unfinished. Amber #e0a33c sun breaking behind the sail, violet-rose #d98fa8 in the high mist. Everything grey except one red, swelling shape arriving. Desire at first sight. PAINTED STILL — no people, no figures, no faces, no hands anywhere in the frame; the place or object IS the subject. Openly erotic metaphor: the shapes, wetness, swelling, thrusting and release unmistakably read as bodies and sex, the way a frank erotic painting does — yet everything stays landscape and object, no nudity, no literal anatomy. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
